builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Training-Adaptive Convolutional Sparse Coding via Information Bottleneck for Robust Visual Representation
summary: The method replaces manually tuned, fixed sparsity coefficients in convolutional sparse coding front-ends with a differentiable coefficient learned jointly with the network via unfolded FISTA iterations, plus a label-free post-training pass that readjusts compression for corrupted inputs. It costs additional inference compute from the iterative FISTA unrolling inside the network, extra training complexity, and an added reconstruction objective that must be balanced against task loss. It can fail if the learned compression strength does not transfer to corruption types unseen during the post-training adjustment, if the iterative unrolling inflates latency beyond budget, or if gains shown on CIFAR/ImageNet classification do not generalize to the reader's task.
rationale: The robustness claim is plausible and implementable on a single 24 GB GPU, but the abstract provides no quantified improvement and the iterative architecture adds latency, so workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.

It costs additional inference compute from the iterative FISTA unrolling inside the network, extra training complexity, and an added reconstruction objective that must be balanced against task loss. Competitive clean-data recognition and greatly improved robustness under input perturbations on CIFAR and ImageNet; no numerical factor is stated in the abstract.
